question: Will at least 450 MEPs vote in favour of the European Parliament's resolution on further EU sanctions against Russia on 12 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: Russia/Ukraine resolutions in the 10th EP term. 4 of the ~10 tallies found reached 450 (469, 482, 492, 541); six fell short (381, 432, 437, 443, 445, 446). The two closest sanctions votes were 446 and 469, either side of the line, and turnout in this term clusters around 560-575 votes cast. The 12 Nov vote is on the Thursday of a Brussels mini-plenary, which tends to mean lower attendance. OEIL gives 11/11 as the indicative date while the agenda says 12/11, and a vote on another day or a postponement resolves No (~10% risk). Starting from ~40% for the reference class, adjusted down for turnout and timing. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.reasoning: Over 14 Russia/Ukraine EP resolutions in 2026, about 5 cleared 450 in favour (479, 480, 482, 492, 541); those were symbolic or condemnation texts with tiny opposition (Duma: 41 against). Sanctions-focused texts have come in below 450: 20th-package resolution 446, Feb 2026 'four years' resolution with sanctions calls 437, Oct 22 Black Sea 432. A 'cutting war financing' text (oil/shadow fleet) draws Patriots opposition and Left/ECR splits. With about 565 voting, 450 needs about 80% yes: reachable but above the sanctions-specific trend. Small extra No-risk from postponement or carry-over. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold per harness; none found in my own searches).

In a Brussels Thursday vote with roughly 560-575 votes cast, a broad joint motion supported by EPP, S&D, Renew, Greens and part of ECR plausibly lands near 440-460, about a coin flip conditional on a recorded vote. With about 560-575 votes cast at a Brussels Thursday sitting, 450 needs about 80% yes. A text on oil and the shadow fleet tends to draw more opposition and abstentions from Patriots, part of ECR and The Left. If a tallied vote happens on 12 Nov, P(>=450) is about 0.38-0.40. calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) vote date 11 vs 12 Nov. The CoP agenda says 12 Nov and outranks the Observatory's indicative date; this can't be verified offline, so I priced about 10-15% risk of no qualifying vote. (2) Show-of-hands precedent from Nov 2024. Current rules can't be confirmed offline; small extra risk. (3) Which comparable tallies count. Run 3's 469 and 460 sanctions-related tallies weaken Run 2's '0 of 3 sanctions texts' framing, so the conditional estimate is about 38-40%. Turnout at a Brussels Thursday sitting (down) is partly offset by the VP election (up). That gives about 0.32.
